global_organization_chain: Summary: emergency -> four-step Model I -> monthly fleets -> GM climate proxy -> three extreme scenarios -> terrain locations -> sensitivity and limits
Front matter: background -> three tasks -> four work products -> global assumptions -> notation -> Model I local assumptions
Base-model interface: fire data -> observed/inferred probability -> personnel -> k-means EOCs -> Kruskal MST -> repeaters -> SSA strategy A/B -> effectiveness
Current-result interface: November/December records -> integrated arrangement -> 73/80 and 80/104 repeater/SSA outputs -> spatial interpretation
Extreme interface: 2011-2020 climate -> GM(1,1) -> 2030 proxy -> Types I-III -> EOC/repeater/SSA changes -> reconciled cost increments
Terrain interface: elevation -> personnel urgency -> EOC movement -> signal obstruction -> SSA route effect -> paired monthly 2D/3D repeater views
Evaluation interface: k sweep -> EOC-count sweep -> tolerance sweep -> strengths -> weaknesses -> conclusion -> continued work -> References -> budget

main_argument_chains.claim: A staged emergency-response model is inspectable only when each operational step consumes typed outputs from the previous one.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Keep a machine-readable handoff ledger before optimizing or budgeting.

main_argument_chains.claim: Fire-location probability can guide predeployment only after the spatial model, training data, and calibration are fully specified.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Treat Equation (2) as an internal score until a real mixture or alternative spatial model is fitted and evaluated.

main_argument_chains.claim: Personnel demand and EOC placement answer different questions and require consistent frequency, coverage, capacity, and cost semantics.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Do not infer minimum EOCs from SSE alone.

main_argument_chains.claim: Short communication trees reduce total length but not necessarily integer repeater demand under heterogeneous terrain ranges.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Compare Kruskal with a terrain-aware minimum-repeater network formulation.

main_argument_chains.claim: Continuous SSA monitoring requires an executable duty timeline, not only a doubled algebraic group count.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Simulate Strategies A and B before treating either fleet count as feasible.

main_argument_chains.claim: A weighted effectiveness score is decision-relevant only when indicator directions, normalization, duplication, and weight order are auditable.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Reconcile Equations (20)-(21) before ranking monthly or sensitivity results.

main_argument_chains.claim: The 73/80 and 80/104 fleets remain internal monthly outputs until inputs, intermediate states, objectives, and solver traces reproduce them.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use reproducible artifact status rather than optimality language.

main_argument_chains.claim: Climate forecasts inform fire planning only through calibrated fire response and out-of-sample forecast evidence.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Treat 26.93 C and 401.81 mm as paper-internal climate proxies, not a fire probability.

main_argument_chains.claim: Composite extreme scenarios reveal system stress but cannot isolate single-factor causes.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Retain the three arithmetic totals while avoiding causal attribution to one changed descriptor.

main_argument_chains.claim: Terrain-aware relay placement requires metric geometry, line-of-sight or diffraction calculations, coordinates, and measured link validation.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Treat Figures 15-16 as illustrative internal locations until their calculations and coordinates are published.

main_argument_chains.claim: One-factor response plots show local direction but cannot establish global robustness of fleet or placement decisions.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Reserve robustness language for interaction-aware uncertainty and decision-stability analysis.

main_argument_chains.claim: A stakeholder budget is auditable only when model quantities, exact arithmetic, quotations, lifecycle costs, uncertainty, and replay evidence reconcile.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The paper supports only an approximate A$2.5 million arithmetic request.
